nodes.label: ADR-0034: Template repositioning, online store scope and derived-app deprecation
nodes.rationale: Defines the scope boundary: full-online website up to online store/e-commerce (catalog, storefront, cart, online checkout as public web surfaces), explicitly excluding in-store POS (physical cashier/offline-first/receipt printing/Coretax) which belongs to the awcms ERP lineage. Supersedes the derived-application pathway (ADR-0013/0014/0015) which is removed by ADR-0036.

nodes.label: ADR-0036: Remove derived application pathway, align family
nodes.rationale: Removes the derived-application pathway (compatibility manifest + extension:check gate) to align AWCMS-Micro with awcms, which already fully removed its derived pathway (PR #205). Supersedes ADR-0035 which had rejected the removal; evidence showed removal possible without reducing test coverage.

nodes.label: ADR-0035 (superseded)
nodes.rationale: Original decision rejecting removal of the derived-application pathway; later superseded by ADR-0036 once evidence showed removal was safe.

nodes.label: ADR-0025: Website scope derivation from awcms-mini
nodes.rationale: Records the reasoning, consequences, and derivation rules for why seven upstream ERP modules (workflow, organization_structure, document_infrastructure, data_exchange, integration_hub, reference_data, idn_admin_regions) are not ported into awcms-micro, since the template's scope is website-only, not ERP back-office.

nodes.label: ADR-0002: Bun-only runtime
nodes.rationale: Mandates Bun as the only backend runtime; Node.js only permitted via documented, maintainer-approved exceptions, to keep tooling and deployment surface minimal and consistent.

nodes.label: ADR-0003: PostgreSQL + RLS multi-tenant
nodes.rationale: Mandates PostgreSQL with Row-Level Security as defense-in-depth for multi-tenant data isolation, enforced even when ABAC already checks access.

nodes.label: ADR-0004: RBAC/ABAC default-deny
nodes.rationale: Security baseline requiring default-deny access control combining RBAC and ABAC, deny overrides allow.

nodes.label: ADR-0011: Capability ports
nodes.rationale: Establishes capability-port pattern so modules can declare/consume cross-cutting capabilities without direct cross-module imports.

nodes.label: ADR-0012: Trusted static module registry
nodes.rationale: Requires the module registry to be a trusted, statically composed set (build-time), not runtime-discovered/uploaded, to avoid arbitrary code/module injection.

nodes.label: ADR-0014: Build-time composition
nodes.rationale: Modules are composed at build time rather than dynamically, ensuring predictable, auditable module sets.

nodes.label: ADR-0027: Full-online deployment and durable storage profiles
nodes.rationale: Defines canonical deployment profiles (development/full_online_single_host/full_online_production) and mandates that production media storage must be durable object storage, not ephemeral container filesystem; clarifies sync_storage is an object queue/outbox, not offline business-data sync. Amends ADR-0006.

nodes.label: ADR-0006: Offline-first sync outbox
nodes.rationale: Original outbox/sync design; later amended by ADR-0027 to reflect full-online deployment reality instead of LAN/offline-first framing.

nodes.label: ADR-0007: OpenAPI/AsyncAPI contracts
nodes.rationale: Mandates API and event contracts be captured formally via OpenAPI and AsyncAPI, kept in sync with implementation.

nodes.label: ADR-0005: Soft delete and immutability
nodes.rationale: Mandates soft-delete for deletable master/config/draft data (deleted_at hidden by default) and immutability for posted/transactional data, corrected only via reversal/adjustment.

nodes.label: ADR-0008: Independent contract and module versioning
nodes.rationale: Decouples package release version (SemVer) from OpenAPI/AsyncAPI contract version and per-module descriptor version/status, each with its own bump policy.
